item: The offline evidence and custody verifiers read a saved bundle as UTF-8 on every OS; on Windows a bundle with non-ASCII text no longer fails as 'signature does not match'
summary: Both verifiers used Path.read_text() with no encoding, i.e. the locale codec (cp1252 on Windows), so an untouched bundle carrying an accented title or a dossier em dash was mangled before verification and reported as tampered. They now read utf-8-sig (a BOM is not JSON, so nothing hashed or signed changes; security read passed), and verify_evidence prints with backslashreplace like verify_custody. Tests run both scripts under an ASCII locale with UTF-8 mode off, and an AST guard makes every file read in scripts/verify_*.py name its encoding. Release line: On Windows, the offline verifiers now verify evidence and custody files containing accented or other non-ASCII text, where before they failed wrongly.
